meta.topic: Why $24,000 invested early beats $72,000 invested late
meta.thesis: At the same return, the first ten years of contributions out-earn thirty later ones, because time compounds the money.
meta.misconception_note: The hook is the misconception flip (more money in must mean more money out); beat 4 shows the contribution gap viewers expect to decide the outcome.

claims.text: Ana invests $200/month from 25 to 35 (120 deposits = $24,000), then stops; at 65 she has about $281,000.
claims.method: FV = P*((1+r)^n-1)/r with r = 7%/12 per month, n = 120, then compounded 360 more months. No fees, taxes or inflation. Hypothetical constant 7% nominal annual return.

claims.text: Ben invests $200/month from 35 to 65 (360 deposits = $72,000); at 65 he has about $244,000.
claims.method: FV = P*((1+r)^n-1)/r with r = 7%/12, n = 360. Same assumptions as c1.

claims.text: At 7% a balance doubles roughly every 10 years (rule of 72: 72/7 = 10.3).
claims.method: Rule of 72 approximation; exact doubling time at 7% annual compounding is 10.24 years.

beats.layer_why: numbers must be exact and animate
beats.visual: two bars slam up: a short one labelled $24K, a tall one labelled $72K; the SHORT one glows

beats.text: Ana invests $200 a month from 25 to 35, then stops.
beats.visual: an age axis 25 to 65; a blue segment fills 25-35 with coin ticks, then goes dark

beats.text: Ben waits until 35, then invests $200 a month until 65.
beats.visual: the same axis; an orange segment fills 35-65 under Ana's row

beats.layer_why: contribution totals are the setup for the twist
beats.text: Ana put in $24,000 total. Ben put in $72,000.
beats.visual: two count-ups roll to $24,000 and $72,000 with Ben's counter running three times as long
both counters freeze, a question mark pulses between them
two growth lines race across the age axis; Ana's curve bends up and overtakes at the end

beats.layer_why: explains the mechanism with an exact rule
beats.text: Her first ten years did most of the work.
beats.visual: Ana's line is highlighted from 35 to 65: no deposits, still climbing

beats.text: At 7%, money doubles about every 10 years.
beats.visual: a coin stack doubles three times along the axis: $34K, $69K, $138K, $281K

beats.layer_why: closes the hook with the reframe
beats.text: Time is the bigger deposit. Start now, even small.
beats.visual: the opening two bars return; the $24K bar now stands taller than the $72K bar
